what:
Log-analysis methodology correction (2026-04-27 user pushback): don't claim absence-of-event from a hook-log paste without explicitly looking for silent-output entries. **Cursor logs every hook fire — even silent ones — as `Hook 1 produced no output` followed by `All hooks for step <name> completed but none returned a valid response`.** These silent entries are visually quiet (no big OUTPUT block, just two timestamped lines) and easy to scroll past. I claimed "Read tool didn't fire on same-session re-read" based on a pasted log section that lacked an explicit preToolUse:Read OUTPUT block — but the silent-fire log lines may have been there or omitted by the paster. User correctly pushed back ("I did see the read call happen again I think you misread").

**Rule going forward when analyzing pasted hook logs:**
1. Don't infer "event didn't fire" from absence of OUTPUT JSON. Look explicitly for the `Hook step requested: <event>` log line — that's the universal "this fired" signal regardless of OUTPUT.
2. If the user says "I saw X happen" and the log doesn't show X, default position is **paste truncation OR my-misreading**, not "X didn't really happen."
3. When in doubt, ask for the full hook log between the two visible boundary events (here: between beforeSubmitPrompt at 15:23:09 and stop at 15:23:21 — 12 seconds where tool calls happened).
4. Same applies to ALL editor hook logs (Claude Code's --debug output, etc.) — silent fires happen for tracked-already-covered cases (correct behavior per memory #324) and are not visible deltas in OUTPUT panels.

**Practical implication for our docs:** the validation matrix should distinguish "hook fired silent (correct because covered)" from "hook didn't fire" explicitly when describing scenarios. Currently sometimes ambiguous — improve when we update E2E_VALIDATION.md.

**Connected to bias directive #358:** the underlying pattern was the same — defaulting to "this thing didn't happen / isn't supported" rather than verifying. Same correction shape: verify before claiming absence.
why: User explicitly corrected me: "I did see the read call happen again I think you misread" — I had claimed Read didn't fire on a same-session re-read based on missing OUTPUT block in the pasted log. Per directive #358 and #344 (validation methodology), I need to default to "I might have missed something / paste might be truncated" rather than "the event didn't happen." Storing as a guideline scoped to validation work so future log-reading sessions don't repeat the same shape of mistake.
